title: Supply Chain Weather Forecast
subtitle: Separate weather stations for declarations under test — no composite risk score.
sourceMode: Signal Translation package on /data/Self-OS origin/master, commit 566d79d2
headline: Declarations are becoming testable claims.
dek: This week's weather is not one score. It is a set of evidence-pressure stations where declared supply-chain records can be compared with observable signals.
forecastHorizon: Now through early September policy clocks

stations.label: Origin observation station
facts: Reuters reported a White House transshipment report estimating $19 billion to $26 billion in annual lost tariff revenue.
The same reporting said CBP is using AI tools to analyze container markings, packaging patterns and X-ray images for mismatches.
The report names about 40 elevated-risk countries, according to the Signal Translation source map.
stations.operatorMeaning: Origin is no longer just a supplier declaration. It needs routing, packaging, marking, broker and approval evidence before the company relies on it.
stations.watch: CBP updates, detention patterns, broker exception logs and any clarified data requirements.

stations.label: Product-attribute station
facts: Commerce is seeking comments by Aug. 27 on additional aluminum, steel and copper derivative articles under Section 232.
Supply Chain Dive summarized 14 proposed derivative categories and rate buckets of 25%, 15% and 50%.
Drone/UAS tariffs include 100%, 25%, 15% and 10% categories and a Sept. 3 effective date in the extracted source notes.
stations.operatorMeaning: HTS, material composition and component provenance have become timed commercial exposure, not static catalog metadata.
stations.watch: Federal Register updates, counsel-reviewed classifications, component-origin evidence and master-data change logs.

stations.label: Flow-split station
stations.condition: Volume, rate and capacity signals disagree
facts: Descartes July U.S. container imports were 2.5 million TEUs, down 4.3% year over year, as reported by Reuters in the source map.
NRF/Hackett June major-port volume was up 13.2% year over year, with July and August forecast declines.
FreightWaves/Xeneta showed Far East-U.S. West Coast and East Coast spot rates falling in the week ending Aug. 13.
stations.operatorMeaning: Physical flow, rate power and demand proof need separate owner cards; do not treat high volume or lower spot rates as proof the route is safe.
stations.watch: Descartes actuals, NRF/Hackett forecasts, Xeneta/FreightWaves rates and port/lane exception logs.

stations.label: Simulation-approval station
facts: Target's Proxima pilot covered 63 fresh-food items, improved on-shelf availability by 2.5%, and simulated the Houston Receive Center at about 98% accuracy.
Reuters reported manufacturers using AI during tariff volatility, with Gartner and McKinsey figures cited through Reuters in the source map.
The Signal Translation package warns that AI should surface mismatches, not approve tariff positions, supplier status or customer promises.
stations.operatorMeaning: Simulation output should become a challenge step with owner, override reason and approval path before inventory moves or promises change.
stations.watch: Pilot accuracy claims, override rules, customer-service impact and measured inventory outcomes.

stations.label: Inland and storage station
facts: Rhine navigable depth at Kaub hit 10 cm on Aug. 14, below the 25 cm 2018 low, with freight shifting to land transport.
India set a maximum daily LPG production target of 63,810 metric tons and required storage/transport capacity directly or through rail and road tankers.
Maharashtra suspended 12 quick-commerce warehouse permits after 86 inspections and 60 improvement notices.
stations.operatorMeaning: Route, storage and capacity claims need current observable evidence; averages are weak when water, permits or inspections change the usable network.
stations.watch: Rhine Kaub levels, storage permits, inspection notices, LPG capacity orders and fallback-route availability.

referenceCards.label: Transshipment estimate
referenceCards.note: White House estimate reported by Reuters; do not treat as independently verified evasion volume.

referenceCards.label: Derivative-duty clock
referenceCards.note: Commerce comment deadline; proposal, not final action.

referenceCards.label: Drone/UAS clock
referenceCards.note: Effective date in secondary Supply Chain Dive summary.

referenceCards.label: July imports
referenceCards.note: Descartes data reported by Reuters; keep separate from NRF/Hackett forecasts.

referenceCards.label: Rhine Kaub depth
referenceCards.note: Reuters Aug. 14 value; capacity stress support, not the thesis.

newsletterInsert.title: Supply Chain Weather
newsletterInsert.headline: Five stations for declarations under test
newsletterInsert.body: This week's weather is not one blended risk score. It is five separate stations where declared records can be compared with observed evidence: origin observation, product attributes, flow split, simulation approval, and inland/storage condition.
newsletterInsert.operatorTranslation: Before approving the next exposed entry, SKU, supplier, route or inventory promise, name the declared claim, the observed surface that could contradict it, the owner, the human approval step and the external watch item.
